brief: JPM's morning briefing argues rates are driving equities. Yesterday's rally in rates supported global equities, and APAC and EU/US futures extend gains. Yields fell on dovish Waller comments and a yen rally, which brought back the debasement trade, with gold and crypto rallying as the dollar weakened. Waller makes September a closer, data-dependent call, markets pricing ~50% chance of a hike versus 65% on Monday, raising event risk into next week's CPI. The yen surge reflects GPIF reallocation speculation and rising BOJ hike expectations, but research calls it overdone and sees USDJPY unlikely to break below the 155-165 range, with the large outstanding JPY short the key risk. Because Asian equity sensitivity to yen appreciation is asymmetric, reduced Asia momentum exposure now sits at levels historically associated with a rebound. Global composite PMI at 53.5 implies 3.1%ar growth, above the 2.3% potential estimate. Positioning is tactically cautious/neutral on global equities, long US and Asia versus EU, bullish EM expressed through country-relative trades, hedged via momentum options and cheap EU index downside.
